subject: music
topicDisplay: The Contemporary Music Maker Hl Project
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In music production, 'multitracking' refers to...?
options: Recording different parts onto separate tracks so they can be balanced and edited independently
Compressing a stereo mix into mono
Playing many instruments live in one take with no overdubs
questions.explain: Multitracking records parts on separate tracks, allowing independent editing and mixing.

questions.q: In composition, developing a musical idea through 'sequence' means...?
options: Repeating a melodic pattern at a higher or lower pitch
questions.explain: A sequence repeats a melodic or harmonic pattern at a different pitch level.

questions.q: Debussy is most closely associated with which musical movement?
questions.explain: Debussy is the leading figure of musical Impressionism, using whole-tone scales and coloured harmonies.

questions.q: A pivot chord in modulation is best defined as which of the following?
options: A chromatic chord with no diatonic function
A chord borrowed from the parallel major
The final chord of a phrase only
A chord common to both the old and new keys used to effect the change
questions.explain: A pivot chord belongs diatonically to both keys, smoothing the transition during a modulation.

questions.q: Early rock 'n' roll of the 1950s (e.g. Chuck Berry) frequently combined the twelve-bar blues with which other key ingredient?
questions.explain: Rock 'n' roll fused the twelve-bar blues with a strong backbeat on beats 2 and 4.

questions.q: Schubert is especially celebrated for his contribution to which genre?
questions.explain: Schubert composed over 600 Lieder, defining the Romantic art song.

questions.q: In Celtic folk music, a 'jig' is most commonly in which metre?
questions.explain: The jig is a lively dance typically in compound 6/8 time.

questions.q: Motown, the Detroit-based label of the 1960s, is associated with which of the following hallmarks?
options: Free improvisation with no fixed form
A polished soul-pop sound with the 'Funk Brothers' house band, tambourine back-beats and call-and-response vocals
questions.explain: Motown produced a slick soul-pop sound built on a house band, back-beat percussion and gospel-derived call-and-response vocals.

questions.q: An appoggiatura is best defined as which?
options: A note approached and left by step
A dissonant note approached by leap and resolved by step
questions.explain: An appoggiatura is an accented non-harmony note usually approached by leap and resolved by step.

questions.q: A diminished seventh chord is built from which stacked intervals?
options: A major third and two minor thirds
questions.explain: The diminished seventh chord consists of three stacked minor thirds, dividing the octave symmetrically.

questions.q: In Indian classical music, a 'raga' is best defined as...?
options: The drone instrument that sustains the tonic
A melodic framework of notes and characteristic phrases used as the basis for improvisation
A fixed rhythmic cycle of beats
questions.explain: A raga is the melodic framework, comprising a set of notes and characteristic phrases, on which improvisation is built.

questions.q: A Picardy third refers to which feature?
options: A chord built on the third degree
A minor-key piece ending on a major (raised third) tonic chord
A third added above the melody
A major piece ending on the minor third
questions.explain: A tierce de Picardie raises the third of the final tonic chord so a minor-key work ends on a major chord.

questions.q: Modal jazz, exemplified by Miles Davis's 'So What', is distinguished from bebop chiefly by its...?
options: Use of static modes/scales held over long stretches rather than frequent chord changes
Reliance on rapid chord changes every two beats
Strict adherence to twelve-bar blues form
questions.explain: Modal jazz bases improvisation on slow-moving modes held for many bars, freeing soloists from rapid chord changes.

questions.q: The technique of word-painting describes which practice?
options: Music that reflects the literal meaning of the text
Painting visual scenery for an opera
questions.explain: Word-painting depicts the meaning of the words in the music, such as rising lines on the word 'ascend'.

questions.q: A 'drone' as a textural device (e.g. in Indian or Celtic music) is...?
options: A sustained note or notes held continuously beneath the melody
questions.explain: A drone is a continuously sustained pitch (or pitches) underpinning the melody.

questions.q: In Indian classical music the term 'bol' refers to...?
options: Mnemonic syllables used to represent and recite drum strokes or rhythms
questions.explain: Bols are spoken mnemonic syllables representing tabla strokes and rhythmic patterns.

questions.q: The dominant of A minor, when used to create a perfect cadence, normally contains which note as its third?
questions.explain: In the harmonic minor the leading note is raised, so E major (the dominant of A minor) contains G sharp.

questions.q: Ragtime, popularised by Scott Joplin, is principally characterised by which rhythmic device?
options: A swung shuffle feel in the bass
A syncopated, off-beat melody set against a steady march-like bass
Continuous polyrhythmic layering of three rhythms
Rubato throughout with no fixed pulse
questions.explain: Ragtime sets a syncopated right-hand melody against a regular, march-style stride bass.

questions.q: In figured bass, the symbol '6' beneath a bass note indicates which chord position?
questions.explain: A bare '6' indicates a first-inversion triad, with the bass note a sixth and a third above it.

questions.q: In ensemble performance, good 'ensemble skills' include all of the following EXCEPT...?
options: Deliberately ignoring the other performers' tempo
Listening and balancing dynamics with other players
Watching for cues and breathing together
Maintaining a shared sense of pulse
questions.explain: Strong ensemble playing depends on listening, balancing and keeping together, not ignoring fellow performers.

questions.q: The 'blue notes' that give the blues scale its characteristic flavour are most typically the flattened third, flattened fifth and flattened...?
questions.explain: The blues scale lowers the third, fifth and seventh degrees, producing the expressive 'blue' inflections.

questions.q: In strict four-part writing, which is a forbidden parallel motion?
questions.explain: Consecutive (parallel) perfect fifths and octaves are prohibited in traditional voice-leading.

questions.q: Chopin's output is dominated by works for which instrument?
questions.explain: Chopin wrote almost exclusively for solo piano, including nocturnes, mazurkas and ballades.

questions.q: In film music, a 'leitmotif' is...?
options: A piece of source music heard within the scene
A recurring musical theme associated with a particular character, place or idea
A sudden silence used for dramatic effect
questions.explain: A leitmotif is a recurring theme linked to a specific character, place or idea, a technique developed by Wagner and used widely in film.

questions.q: The interval from C up to G is which?
questions.explain: C up to G spans seven semitones, a perfect fifth.

questions.q: The studio effect 'reverb' is used to...?
options: Speed up the tempo of a track
Simulate the natural reflections of a sound in a space, adding sense of depth/ambience
Shift the pitch of a vocal up an octave
questions.explain: Reverb recreates the reflections of a physical space, adding depth and ambience to a sound.

questions.q: The compositional device of 'augmentation' refers to...?
options: Raising the pitch of a theme
Lengthening the note values of a theme, usually doubling them
questions.explain: Augmentation lengthens a theme's note values, typically doubling each duration.

questions.q: A secondary dominant such as V of V in C major would be which chord?
questions.explain: In C major, the dominant is G, and the dominant of G (V of V) is a D major chord.

questions.q: Sonata form consists of which three main sections?
questions.explain: Sonata form unfolds in exposition, development and recapitulation, often with an introduction and coda.

questions.q: The Indonesian 'gamelan' is primarily an ensemble of...?
questions.explain: A gamelan is built chiefly from tuned metallophones, gongs and drums.
